sections.what: Acts as the front door of the programme package. Other code can get the programme data types and the builder function from here without knowing which internal file defines them.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes outside imports short and stable if internal files are moved or split.
sections.watch_out: Keep the export list and the import lines in sync, or the package will fail to import.

summary: This file is the public entry point for the programme package. It gathers the programme data shapes and the builder function so other code can import them from one place.
purpose: Gives other parts of the app a single, stable import location for programme data types and the builder.
why: Likely reason: keeps outside imports short and stable if internal file layout changes. Reason not stated in the code.
how: It imports four data shape classes from the contracts file and the builder function from the service file, then lists those five names in an export list that defines what the package offers.
inputs: None at run time. It only loads other modules when the package is first imported.
outputs: The five names listed in the export list, available for import.
risks: Importing this package also loads the service file, so an error in the service file will also break anything that imports only the contracts.
debug: If an import of the programme package fails, check the import lines at the top of this file, then open the named file and look for the error.
